author: Kusha N M
raw:
ನಾಳೆಮಾಡುವೆನೆನಲು ನಗುವ ಮೊದಲಿಗೆ ದೇವ
ಸೀಳುಭೂಮಿಯ ಭಾಗ ನನದಾಗಲೆನಲು
ಬೀಳುತಿಹ ದೇಹವನು ತಾನುಳಿಪೆನೆಂದಾಗ
ಶೂಲಪಾಣಿಯು ನಗುವ ಮೂಢಮನುಜ

lines: When you say “I will do it tomorrow”, God is the first to laugh;
when you say “let this divided piece of land be mine”,
when you say you will save this falling body,
the trident-bearer laughs, O deluded one.
en.note: The verse echoes the well-known saying of Śrī Rāmakṛṣṇa that God laughs when brothers divide their land, and when a physician promises to save a life. Śūlapāṇi, “trident-bearer”, is Śiva.
en.bhavartha: Putting things off till tomorrow, staking claims to pieces of land, promising to save a body that is bound to fall: to the divine, these are all laughable. We are not in charge of time, property or life.
